\section*{Question 5}

The graph of the function \(f\) shown above consists of a semicircle and three line segments. Let \(g\) be the function given by \(g(x)=\int_{-3}^{x} f(t) d t\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find \(g(0)\) and \(g^{\prime}(0)\).
\item[(b)] Find all values of \(x\) in the open interval (-5, 4) at which \(g\) attains a relative maximum. Justify your answer.
\item[(c)] Find the absolute minimum value of \(g\) on the closed interval [-5, 4]. Justify your answer.
\item[(d)] Find all values of \(x\) in the open interval (-5, 4) at which the graph of \(g\) has a point of inflection.
\item[(a)] \(\quad g(0)=\int_{-3}^{0} f(t) d t=\frac{1}{2}(3)(2+1)=\frac{9}{2}\) \(g^{\prime}(0)=f(0)=1\)
\item[(b)] \(g\) has a relative maximum at \(x=3\).
This is the only \(x\)-value where \(g^{\prime}=f\) changes from positive to negative.
\item[(c)] The only \(x\)-value where \(f\) changes from negative to positive is \(x=-4\). The other candidates for the location of the absolute minimum value are the endpoints.
\[
\begin{aligned}
& g(-5)=0 \\
& g(-4)=\int_{-3}^{-4} f(t) d t=-1 \\
& g(4)=\frac{9}{2}+\left(2-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{13-\pi}{2}
\end{aligned}
\]
So the absolute minimum value of \(g\) is -1 .
\item[(d)] \(x=-3,1,2\)
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: g(0) \\ 1: g^{\prime}(0)\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: x=3 \\ 1: \text { justification }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { identifies } x=-4 \text { as a candidate } \\ 1: g(-4)=-1 \\ 1: \text { justification and answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[2] : correct values
\(\langle-1\rangle\) each missing or extra value
\end{itemize}
